summary: A 1917 47-ft steel Aermotor LS40 replaced a 1912 wooden station tower on Belfry Mountain; fire watch ended 1988, state closure followed; still standing with radio gear.

access.note: Site is accessible to the public on a DEC-recommended trail. No source confirms the tower is open for climbing; it was officially closed as a fire tower in 1989.

notes_for_editor: Build history is consistent across sources only at the level of a 1912 station with a wooden tower and a 1917 steel tower. NHLR lists 1917 as the build year, which the brief also uses; Wikipedia and the Explorer say 1917 replaced a 1912 wooden tower. Closure date conflicts: NHLR says closed 1988; Wikipedia says out of service 1988 and officially closed early 1989; Stream & Steeple agrees with Wikipedia. Ownership conflicts: NHLR says administered by NYSDEC and the Explorer places it in the Hammond Pond Wild Forest, but Stream & Steeple says private land. Trail length conflicts (0.3 vs 0.4 mile). Access is set to public for the site only; no source confirms that climbing the tower is permitted, and the story advises treating it as closed. Stream & Steeple lists Belfry in an ADK Fire Tower Challenge that requires climbing fire tower summits; that is not a state opening. Staffing history rests on the Explorer's 'until 1988' and the 2017 visit report; the Podskoch book and the Landmarks of Moriah post were not reachable. andyarthur.org pages returned HTTP 403 and were not used. The height is converted from 47 feet. Verification pass 2026-10-08: the story's 'site is open to the public' wording was changed to the tower being accessible, as Stream & Steeple states; the 'no source says climbers' sentence was corrected for the challenge text; 'cab glass broken' was changed to 'not intact' to match the form.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR's 1917 build year refers to the steel tower. Wikipedia, the Weebly history page and the Explorer record a station and wooden tower from 1912, which the story reports as the first structure.
NHLR says closed 1988; Wikipedia and Stream & Steeple say out of service 1988 and officially closed early 1989. The story reports both.
NHLR says administered by NYSDEC and the Explorer places it in the Hammond Pond Wild Forest; Stream & Steeple says private lands. The story states the state-land account and flags the disagreement.
Stream & Steeple lists Belfry in an ADK challenge that requires climbing fire tower summits; no source says the state has opened the tower to climbers. The story treats the tower as closed.
